critic.summary: I re-read the plan plain text (sections 2-5, 13-19, 21, 24 and cards N01-N11, S01-S04), the runbook, AGENTS.md, redovi.json, master-plan-live-state.json, the EX-06 scope doc, the legal-drafts README, OWNER_INPUTS_NEEDED and PLAN.md. I also read the relevant source files and ran read-only catalog and count queries on DEV (counts and function and policy definitions only). I found no refutation of the core facts the reports share: P7-only rows are N01-N11 plus S01 and S02, EX-07 has no scope record, and DEV has never exercised any account flow. I found gaps in four places. (1) Requirements: the only canonical rule that defines "active fake command" is runbook 2.1, and no report cites it. Plan 3.1 also makes "basic safety/account operations" mandatory V1 scope, so hiding report or support is not a free option. The runbook first-entry exit criteria and plan 13.1's "ratings, Dogovori and finished jobs" overview are unchecked, and the hub has no such overview. (2) New concrete contradictions: eas.json production env points at the DEV project; the legal registry holds only TERMS and PRIVACY and requires an https URL; the blocked-list name is chosen REQUESTER-first, which can differ from the name the blocker saw; AGENTS 3.1.3 against 3.1.2; and the reports disagree among themselves on whether any misleading copy exists. (3) Several "CONFIRMED EXISTS" findings are really SOURCE plus catalog plus disposable-CI. Live DEV re-read: 0 legal documents, 0 acceptances, 0 operator grants and 0 closures, with ready=true and digest 58447d77. (4) The gates that bind EX-07 are: "primeni" per package, certificate re-bind, legal/company data, external accounts and paid resources, DEV writes and new test accounts, phone sign-out limits, push, and dependencies. Biggest unsettled decision: what "no active fake command" means, since nothing canonical defines it beyond runbook 2.1.
